title: Ten Minutes After the Walk: What Exercise Really Does to a Bad Morning
title_zh: 走完那十分钟之后：运动究竟对糟糕的早晨做了什么
intro_zh: 本文约534词，含6个CET-4核心新词，句子难度中等（3/5），理解难度目标为85%-90%。文章从大脑化学物质、运动时长、场地环境、社交因素和“练过头”的误区几个具体角度，说明运动为什么能改善心情。

paragraphs.en: Think of a morning when everything went wrong: a failed quiz, a missed bus, cold coffee spilt on your notes. You decided to walk to the next building instead of waiting for the shuttle. Ten minutes later, the day still had the same problems, but it no longer felt heavy. Nothing about your timetable had changed. Only your body had moved, and that was enough to shift something.
paragraphs.zh: 想一想某个事事不顺的早晨：小测没过，公交错过，冷咖啡洒在了笔记上。你决定不等人挤校车，直接走到下一栋楼去。十分钟后，这一天的问题还是那些问题，但它不再那么沉重了。你的日程表没有发生任何变化，只是你的身体动了起来，而这就足以改变点什么。

paragraphs.en: Scientists have a name for part of this process. When you move, your muscles and brain release a group of chemicals that ease pain and lift mood. Endorphins are the famous ones, but dopamine and serotonin matter just as much. They do not make your problems disappear. They change how hard those problems press on you.
paragraphs.zh: 科学家为这一过程的一部分起了名字。当你运动时，肌肉和大脑会释放一组减轻疼痛、提振心情的化学物质。内啡肽是其中最出名的，但多巴胺和血清素同样重要。它们并不会让你的问题消失，而是改变了这些问题压在你身上的力度。

paragraphs.en: One reason exercise is so reliable is that the effect starts fast. A large review of studies covering more than 30,000 people found that even a single session of light activity — a short walk, a slow bike ride — could reduce anxiety within minutes. The biggest improvements appeared in people who were already under stress. The change came within the first hour, and it did not depend on how fit they were.
paragraphs.zh: 运动之所以如此可靠，原因之一是效果来得快。一项涵盖三万多人研究的综述发现，哪怕只进行一次轻量活动——一段短走、一次慢骑——也能在几分钟内降低焦虑。改善最明显的是那些本来就处于压力中的人。这种变化在第一个小时内就出现了，而且与他们的体能好坏无关。

paragraphs.en: Duration matters less than most people think. Ten to fifteen minutes of movement is often enough to boost mood, especially if the movement is gentle and steady rather than exhausting. You do not need a gym membership or a perfect plan to feel the benefit. Stairs instead of the lift, a walk after lunch, two songs of dancing in your room — all of these count.
paragraphs.zh: 时长没有大多数人想的那么重要。十到十五分钟的活动往往就足以提升心情，尤其是当这种活动温和而持续、而不是让人精疲力竭时。你不需要健身卡，也不需要完美的计划，就能感受到好处。不坐电梯走楼梯、午饭后散一段步、在房间里跟着两首歌跳舞——这些都算数。

paragraphs.en: Where you move also matters. Walks in a park or along a river seem to work better than the same walk on a treadmill. Researchers call this 'green exercise', and studies suggest that as little as five minutes in a natural setting can lower stress. Trees, daylight and open space give your attention a rest, and a rested mind is a calmer one. Even a view of trees from a window helps a little.
paragraphs.zh: 你在哪里运动也很重要。在公园里或沿河散步，似乎比在跑步机上走同样一段路效果更好。研究者称之为“绿色运动”，研究显示，在自然环境中只要待上五分钟就能降低压力。树木、日光和开阔的空间让你的注意力得到休息，而得到休息的大脑会更平静。哪怕只是从窗口看看树，也有一点帮助。

paragraphs.en: There is a social side, too. People who move with a friend or a small group tend to report better moods than those who always train alone. Talking, laughing and keeping a simple promise to meet someone add a second layer of help that no app can copy. A twenty-minute walk with a classmate after dinner can be exercise and friendship at the same time. You also tend to walk further without noticing.
paragraphs.zh: 还有社交的一面。和朋友或小群体一起运动的人，往往比总是独自锻炼的人心情更好。聊天、大笑，以及守住一个“见面”的简单约定，构成了第二层帮助，这是任何手机应用都复制不了的。晚饭后和同学走二十分钟，既是运动，也是友情。而且你往往会不知不觉走得更远。

paragraphs.en: The catch is that more is not always better. Training too hard, too often, or treating exercise as a punishment for eating can leave people tired, injured and guiltier than before. If a workout makes you dread the next one, it is too big. The aim is not to burn a number on a screen; it is to finish feeling a little lighter than when you started.
paragraphs.zh: 问题在于，练得多并不总是更好。练得太猛、太频繁，或者把运动当成对“吃了东西”的惩罚，会让人更疲惫、受伤，也比以前更有负罪感。如果一次锻炼让你害怕下一次，那它就过量了。目标不是在屏幕上烧掉一个数字，而是结束时比开始时感觉轻松一点。

paragraphs.en: So keep the plan small and repeatable. Choose one moment in your day — after class, before dinner — and attach ten minutes of movement to it. Notice how you feel afterwards, not how many calories you burned. Over a few weeks, those short walks and stretches quietly build a mood that is steadier and a body that is easier to live in.
paragraphs.zh: 所以，把计划定得小一点、可重复一点。在一天中挑一个时刻——下课后、晚饭前——给它挂上十分钟的活动。运动结束后去留意自己的感受，而不是烧掉了多少卡路里。几周之后，这些短短的散步和拉伸会安静地为你攒出一种更稳定的心情，和一副住起来更舒服的身体。

questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Why professional athletes train harder than other people.
How different kinds of physical activity can lift a person's mood.
How to design a perfect weekly exercise plan for students.
Why young people today feel more stress than before.
questions.explain: 主旨题。全文从大脑化学物质、单次运动的效果、时长、场地、社交因素和过量运动的危险等角度，说明不同类型的身体活动如何改善心情，故选B。A、C、D均非文章重点。

questions.q: What did the large review of studies find?
options: Only intense exercise has any effect on mood.
Exercise improves mood only after several weeks of training.
A single short session of light activity can lower anxiety within minutes.
People who exercise regularly never feel anxious.
questions.explain: 细节题。第三段明确说，涵盖三万多人研究的综述发现，哪怕一次轻量活动也能在几分钟内降低焦虑，故选C。A与“轻量活动也有效”相反，B与“效果来得快”相反，D为绝对化表述，文中未提。

questions.q: Why does the author mention walks in a park?
options: To show that where you exercise can add to its effect on mood.
To suggest that indoor exercise is harmful to health.
To prove that fresh air can completely cure a low mood.
To explain why parks are cheaper than gyms.
questions.explain: 推断题。第五段以公园散步对比跑步机，并引入“绿色运动”概念，说明运动场地会给心情带来额外的益处，故选A。文中说室内运动“效果稍逊”，并未说有害，也没有“彻底治愈”或费用比较的说法。

questions.q: The word 'catch' in paragraph 7 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: 词义题。第七段先说“练得多并不总是更好”，随后列举练过猛带来的疲惫、受伤和负罪感，可见 the catch 指“隐藏的问题、隐患”，故选B。A只是后文举例之一，C、D与上下文逻辑不符。
